tools.name: highlyt_get_highlight_links
tools.title: Get Highlight Links

tools.description:
Create a link between two highlights to form an insight thread.
Supports both same-document and cross-document linking.

IMPORTANT — parent/child semantics:
- parent_highlight_id = the highlight you are viewing (the "context" highlight)
- child_highlight_id = the highlight you are linking TO (the "related" highlight)
- link_type describes what the CHILD does to the PARENT:
  - supports: "child supports parent" (child provides evidence for parent)
  - contradicts: "child contradicts parent" (child challenges parent)
  - expands: "child expands parent" (child elaborates on parent)
  - questions: "child questions parent" (child raises questions about parent)
  - related: general connection

For cross-document links, set target_document_id to the document containing the
child highlight. If omitted, both highlights are assumed to be in source_document_id.

Example: If highlight A says "GDP grew 5%" and you want to link highlight B
"Exports increased 12%" as supporting evidence, then:
  parent_highlight_id = A (the claim), child_highlight_id = B (the evidence),
  link_type = "supports" (B supports A).

params.description: Parameters for creating a link between two highlights (same-doc or cross-doc).

source_document_id.description: UUID of the source document containing the parent highlight

target_document_id.description: UUID of the target document for cross-document links. If omitted, same-document link.

parent_highlight_id.description: The highlight you are viewing or working on (the 'context' highlight). The link_type describes what the child does TO this highlight.

child_highlight_id.description: The highlight you are linking TO (the 'related' highlight). This highlight performs the action described by link_type on the parent.

link_type.description: Describes what the child does to the parent. 'supports' = child provides evidence for parent. 'contradicts' = child challenges parent. 'expands' = child elaborates on parent. 'questions' = child raises questions about parent. 'related' = general connection.

tools.description:
List all cluster summaries for a document's knowledge graph.

Returns each summary with its highlight_ids array — the highlights that were
in the cluster when the summary was last generated.

DETECTING STALE SUMMARIES:
To check if summaries need updating after adding new links:
1. Call highlyt_list_highlight_links to get all current links
2. Compute connected components (group highlights by connectivity)
3. Call this tool to get stored summaries
4. For each summary, check if its highlight_ids is a SUBSET of a current component
   - If highlight_ids == component_ids → summary is current
   - If highlight_ids ⊂ component_ids → summary is STALE (cluster grew)
   - Set difference (component_ids - highlight_ids) = newly added highlights
5. Regenerate stale summaries with highlyt_upsert_cluster_summary,
   passing the FULL current component highlight_ids

params.description: Parameters for listing cluster summaries.

tools.name: highlyt_list_cluster_summaries
tools.title: List Cluster Summaries

tools.description:
Create or update a summary for a connected component cluster in the knowledge graph.

A cluster is a group of linked highlights that form a connected component.

IMPORTANT:
- highlight_ids must be the COMPLETE, CURRENT set of highlight UUIDs in the cluster
  (not just newly added ones). The array is sorted internally for matching.
- If a summary already exists for this document_id + highlight_ids combination,
  it will be UPDATED (upsert behavior).
- When updating a stale summary (cluster grew due to new links), pass the FULL
  updated highlight_ids array so the stored record reflects the current cluster.
- The summary should describe thematic connections across ALL highlights in the cluster,
  including any newly added ones.

Typical workflow:
1. Read highlights with highlyt_list_highlights
2. Read links with highlyt_list_highlight_links
3. Compute connected components from links
4. For each component, generate a summary covering all highlights
5. Call this tool with the component's highlight_ids and generated summary

params.description: Parameters for creating or updating a cluster summary.

document_id.description: UUID of the document containing the highlights

highlight_ids.description: Complete list of highlight UUIDs forming the connected component cluster. Must include ALL highlights currently in the cluster, not just new ones. The array is sorted internally for deterministic matching.

summary.description: Summary describing the thematic connections and relationships across ALL highlights in the cluster. Should cover how the highlights relate to each other and their collective significance.

title.description: Short descriptive title for the cluster (e.g., 'Economic Growth Evidence', 'Competing Theories on X')

tools.name: highlyt_upsert_cluster_summary
tools.title: Upsert Cluster Summary

tools.description:
Retrieve images (charts, graphs, figures, diagrams, photos) and their surrounding
text context from an EPUB or web clip document.

WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
- User asks about a chart, graph, figure, diagram, or image in a document
- User wants visual data or illustrations from a book/article
- User references "Figure X.X" or any visual element

Returns each image's base64 data URI, alt text, dimensions, chapter location,
and the paragraph text before/after it so you can describe what the image shows.
Use the optional query parameter to filter images by surrounding text context.

For PDFs, images are embedded in the rendered pages — use highlyt_get_page_text instead.

params.description: Parameters for retrieving images and their surrounding context from EPUB/web documents.

query.description: Optional search query to filter images by surrounding text context (e.g., 'chart revenue growth')

page_end.description: End page number. Defaults to page_start + 4 (max 5 pages per request).

tools.description:
Full-text search across your entire library — documents, highlights, and page content.

This searches the actual text content of your PDFs (every page), highlight text/comments,
and document metadata (title, author, keywords). Results are ranked by relevance with
text snippets showing where matches were found.

Supports natural language queries and websearch syntax:
- Simple: "machine learning"
- Exact phrase: '"neural network"'
- OR: "neural OR deep"
- Exclude: "learning -supervised"

Each result includes match_type ('content', 'highlight', or 'metadata'),
the page number where the match was found, and a snippet with **bold** markers
around matching terms.

params.description: Parameters for full-text search across all document content.

query.description: Search query. Supports natural language and websearch syntax (e.g. 'machine learning', '"exact phrase"', 'neural OR deep')

scope.description: Search scope: 'all' (default), 'content' (page text only), 'highlights' (highlights only), or 'metadata' (title/author/keywords only)

document_id.description: Limit search to a specific document UUID

shelf_id.description: Limit search to documents on a specific shelf UUID

tools.name: highlyt_search
tools.title: Full-Text Library Search
